guide.summary: A tiny parasite that clings to fungus threads and drains them.
guide.biology: Threadrider is made up, inspired by real parasites that feed on the threads of fungi.
guide.rules: Lives free in gel or sediment, where it cannot feed: it moves 0.3 cells per second, senses hosts up to 3 cells away and pays 0.12 energy per second. It attaches only to active Cordweaver or Sporeveil segments, one parasite per segment, and never to a resting Sporeveil daughter. It drains 0.015 carbon per second, never more than the segment has, and needs no oxygen: half becomes Threadrider body, 0.30 carbon dioxide and 0.20 metabolite, and it gains 30 energy per carbon. A segment below a quarter of its starting body dies. If its segment dies or rests, Threadrider is released alive nearby and must find another host before it starves. It never travels along fungal transport links. Lives up to 360 seconds.
guide.example: Add Threadriders to a growing Cordweaver network and compare how far it spreads with and without them.
